correctness.rationale: Unique factorization assigns the exponent k+j to each prime of nonzero residual exponent j and puts the remaining kth powers into a; thus every nonpower has one ray. Each p is below 1/2, and summability follows by dropping squarefreeness and taking the product of zeta sums. The hit phases for a ray are the open arc (1-p,1); the wraparound and ordinary intersections with the translated arc give the two terms of g_p. Lemma 2 of arXiv:2512.07438 supplies precisely the independence including 1 needed for finite-coordinate equidistribution. Counting omitted-ray roots up through N+t+1 bounds the n-average error by 2(N+t+1)/N times the omitted sum; t is fixed here. In the separate lag average, telescoping differences of the finite and infinite products gives a uniform error controlled by four times the omitted sum, allowing continuous tests. The phase product is continuous on the compact connected torus, with range between the two attainable endpoint products and full Haar-image support; weak convergence and the range bound imply the whole cluster set. The overlap has a zero atom of mass 1-2p and a positive part uniform on (0,p) after conditioning. The minimum product occurs only when all overlaps are zero; on the complement, partition by the first positive overlap and condition on all other coordinates. The other factors have positive product, so this gives a density. The two-wing integrals are p² and 2p³/3, giving the stated mean and variance, with a strictly positive local variance and a positive remaining product. The support crosses zero because 0<C_k<D_k²<D_k<1. The cited summability equation number appears to be (12), not (10), in the retrieved paper, and the frozen proof also gives its own valid zeta bound. The frozen verify_autocorrelation.py and VERIFICATION.md describe finite squarefull-ray and local integral checks; these are corroboration only, not used as the analytic proof or independently executed.
